summary: L04-SPEC-04, the one item round 2 left open (a door that actually replaces a schedule after a term correction, named by #939 AC4 / #941 AC3), is built in this round and I verified it is real. Read both tickets fresh (gh issue view 939/941 --json body,comments): #939 has zero comments, #941 has two and neither touches AC3/AC4/decision 3, so the Agent Brief text the fix-3 report quotes is still the newest word on this. The quoted sentences match verbatim: #939 AC4 'a new schedule from the next period is the only correction path; a cell proves posted occurrences and their receipts are unchanged', #939 decision 3 'already-posted periods are never touched', #941 AC3 the same clause and its cell list naming 'a term correction'. Round 3's reading -- that 'the only correction path' names an act that must exist, not just a prohibition -- is the more literal reading of the ticket text and I did not find a later ruling that contradicts it. New migration 0317_schedule_term_correction.sql (2717 lines on disk, not the 2691 the report states -- a harmless miscount, not a structural gap) has the house shape: a numbered prestate DO block that measures six recut bodies' sha256(prosrc) and two neighbour-body pin arrays live on clara_l04 before editing anything, the change (supersession columns, partial unique indexes replacing the two unconditional ones, two new doors, two ungranted predicates, four recut bodies with one predicate added each), and a tail DO block re-measuring all of it (qualified uniqueness, bidirectional chain integrity, the four recut bodies' live predicate, the two triggers' stamp admission, owner/definer/search_path/volatility posture, the full ACL matrix by has_function_privilege, a zero-count catalog scan proving no wake wrapper or OBO twin exists, and a byte-exact re-check of every kept neighbour). The gate module tests/schedule-term-correction-preintegration-gate.mjs is the LAST entry in packages/db/package.json's --import chain, immediately after tests/prepayment-wake-reroute-preintegration-gate.mjs (0315's own gate) -- migration order is correct. rig-meta.mjs carries SCHEDULE_TERM_CORRECTION_0317_COHORT (two human doors, two ungranted predicates) wired into the live-roster census. I independently re-measured the ledger: on clara_l04, select version, checksum from clara.schema_migrations shows 0317_schedule_term_correction at 613c6486b65e9f80c5ef67a6caca3ed8e5476440f7276822968c96a4b3f4e904, which I recomputed myself from the on-disk file with the same CRLF-normalised sha256 recipe migrate.mjs uses and it matches exactly. I independently queried pg_proc/aclexplode for both new doors (not trusting only the migration's own tail assertions): both are owned by clara_fn_owner, prosecdef=true, search_path=clara,pg_temp, and EXECUTE is granted to exactly clara_fn_owner (owner) and clara_authenticated -- no clara_runtime, no wake role, no clara_agent_ro, matching the report's claim and matching p939.replace.posture's own re-measurement (which I also re-ran green). I drove the door for real rather than only reading code: running the full 112-entry gate chain against tests/prepayment-stated-term.test.mjs + tests/revenue-recognition.test.mjs on clara_l04 gives 31 tests, 31 pass, 0 fail, exactly the fix-3 report's claim -- and that run genuinely exercises AC4/AC3: p939.replace.posted takes one occurrence through the real wake/claim/post/settle chain to a COMMITTED receipt, corrects the term, calls the door, and the replacement starts the day after the admitted month (admitted_periods=1, admitted_cents=22500, first_open_period_start the next month), re-spreads the remaining 67500 over three months at 22500 each with admitted_cents + total_cents = 90000 (nothing lost, nothing doubled), and the admitted occurrence and its committed receipt read back byte-identical afterwards -- AC4's own sentence, driven rather than asserted. p939.replace.refuses and p941.replace.refuses (both green in the same run) cover: a term nobody corrected (term_live, naming the stating door), a re-statement that moved neither date (term_unmoved), a blank reason, a viewer (CLR.authz), a schedule naming nothing, and a schedule already replaced (naming its successor). p939.replace.boundary covers the two edges of the prospective rule (corrected term ending inside the taken-up month; every month already taken up), both refusing by name and naming admitted_periods/admitted_cents. The one axis the recheck prompt asked for that is not independently live-driven this round is 'refused to another firm': no cell calls the door with a real cross-firm schedule id (only nowhereId(), a random UUID, which proves absent, not foreign). I read the body instead (0317:536, 0317:932): both loads are 'where s.id = p_schedule and s.client_id = p_client and s.firm_id = v_firm', the identical firm-scoped shape every other door in this lane uses and that the adversarial review already drove for sibling doors with no existence oracle found -- so absent and foreign do answer alike by construction, but this round did not re-prove it empirically for these two specific functions. On the OBO-twin question: 0317 deliberately builds no twin for either door (grant to clara_authenticated only), which is a different posture from #915's clara.create_prepayment_schedule_for (a separate function, clara_runtime only). I checked these are not in tension: #939 decision 6 already ruled the term-stating door gets no agent grant and no wake wrapper ('the model can only ask the fixed two-date question; it never supplies dates'), and 0317's correction door carries the identical reasoning forward -- a term correction is the same class of judgement as stating the term, so the human-door-only shape is the CONSISTENT one, not a deviation from #915's shape (#915's door is a different act, configuring a schedule from an already-recorded term, which the ticket explicitly opened to the machine lane). On the accounting question: MPERS section 10 / MFRS 108 is the right family of standard for a prospective-change-in-estimate-vs-error question, and characterising a term correction as a change in estimate (rather than a prior-period error requiring restatement) is consistent with the owner's own 2026-09-18 decision 3 ('already-posted periods are never touched') -- the fix-3 report is restating a business rule the owner already made in the correct vocabulary, not inventing a new professional judgement. The 120-month cap is not re-implemented in 0317, and I confirmed that is deliberate and sound: the corrected term must already pass ck_pst_max_periods/ck_dsp_max_periods at the recording door (0140/0305) before the correction door ever sees it, and clara.prepayment_schedule_v2 enforces the same cap a second time on whatever it is handed -- a third cap in 0317 would be a third copy of the same rule. I re-ran the full regression surface beyond the two lane-specific files: the wider set (prepayment-wake-reroute, prepayment-stated-term, prepayment-account-roster, prepayment-schedule, prepayment-schedule-obo, revenue-recognition, plan-overlap-template-arm-retired, f-a4-pr2a-books, f-a4-pr2a-wrapper, f-a4-pr2a-census, f-a4-pr2a-schedule, operation-census, rig-isolation) gives 142 tests, 141 pass, 0 fail, 1 skip (the known destructive-reset skip) -- exact match to fix-3's own count, confirming every finding both earlier recheck rounds accepted (L04-SPEC-01/02/03, STD-1, ADV-01..08, L04-SPEC-05/06/07/08/09, STD-2) is still fixed and nothing regressed. pnpm typecheck is clean. CI=true GITHUB_ACTIONS=true pnpm lint exits 0 (captured directly). check-frozen-workflows.mjs: OK, 312 files, 0 diff. check-parts-parity.mjs: OK. apps/web whole unit suite: 5035 tests, 5033 pass, 0 fail, 2 skipped -- exact match. Both Playwright walks on the lane's own triple (https://127.0.0.1:3530 / 3531 / 3532) pass: prepayments-walk 8/8, deferred-revenue-walk 3/3 (my first attempt at these collided because I ran both concurrently against the same ports without setting the triple's env vars -- a mistake in my own process, not evidence of anything in the branch; re-run sequentially with the correct env vars, both green). git status --short is empty throughout and at the end. Nothing above minor remains: this round closes the one major every prior round carried forward, and does so with genuine coverage rather than a narrower reading of the acceptance criteria.

still_open.note: fix-3's report states the new migration is 2691 lines; wc -l on the actual file gives 2717. Cosmetic miscount in the report prose, not a structural or content defect -- the file's sha256 matches the DB ledger exactly regardless of the stated line count.

Neither p939.replace.refuses/boundary/posture nor my own session drove the correction door with a real cross-firm schedule id (only nowhereId(), a random UUID, proving absent rather than foreign). The body's WHERE clause is firm-scoped identically to every sibling door in this lane (confirmed by reading 0317:536 and 0317:932), and the adversarial review already proved the no-existence-oracle property for sibling doors sharing this exact shape, so this is architecturally sound rather than an open question -- but it was verified by code inspection this round, not by a fresh live cross-firm drive of these two specific functions. Worth a one-line cell in a future pass, not a blocker.
